reading.text:
# Reading of §2 ¶1, separability (sec2_separable)

Passage: "ν is a σ-finite measure on a countably generated (E, 𝓔) (so that L²(ν;ℝʲ) is
separable for every j ≥ 1)".

A faithful formal statement: for every measurable space (E, 𝓔) that is countably generated and
every σ-finite measure ν on it, and every j ≥ 1 (j = 0 harmless), the space L²(ν;ℝʲ) (Lebesgue
L² classes of ℝʲ-valued functions, Euclidean norm) is a separable topological (metric) space.
No further hypotheses. (Separability of the Bochner space with norm topology.)

comparison.text:
# Comparison for sec2_separable

Lean: ∀ E, ν σ-finite, E countably generated, j ≥ 1: SeparableSpace (Lp (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin j))
2 ν).

- Hypotheses: σ-finite ν on a countably generated measurable space. Match.
- j ≥ 1. Match.
- L²(ν; ℝʲ): Mathlib Lp with the Euclidean norm on ℝʲ, norm topology. Separability of the
  topological space. Match.
- No hypotheses to witness beyond existence of such ν (e.g. any finite measure on ℝ).

Verdict: faithful.

author_review.disagreements:
For sec2_separable itself: none.
On the joint §2 review shown here (which also covers eq_compid, eq_zeromean, sec2_prp,
sec2_infinite_activity, sec2_hborel, whose own author entries displayed empty): one imprecision.
It reads `markedPredictableSigma` as "the σ-algebra 𝒫 ⊗ ℰ generated by F × (r, q] × B with
F ∈ ℱ_r". The generators also require r ≥ 0 and ν(B) < ∞; with ν σ-finite this is 𝒫 ⊗ ℰ on
times > 0, but the region of times ≤ 0 (including time 0, where the paper's 𝒫 contains
{0} × F₀ × B) is unsplit, so measurable integrands are constant there. Harmless for (2.1)–(2.2)
since all integrals run over (0, T], but the review should say so rather than identify the two
σ-algebras.
